examples.ko: 인접 국가들과 사이좋게 지내는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: It is important to get along with neighboring countries.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 인접 도시로 출퇴근하기 편해요.
examples.en: My home is convenient for commuting to the nearby city.
I heard the same thing happened in the neighboring area.

examples.ko: 인접 건물에 불이 번져서 큰일 날 뻔했어요.
examples.en: The fire spread to the adjacent building and it almost became serious.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 인접 관계라서 교류가 많아요.
examples.en: The two countries are neighbors, so they have a lot of exchange.

examples.ko: 인접 학교끼리 모여서 체육 대회를 열어요.
examples.en: Nearby schools gather together to hold a sports day.

explain: 인접은 혼자 쓰기보다 '인접 국가', '인접 지역', '인접 건물'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여서 써요. '옆', '가까운'보다 딱딱해서 뉴스·지도·공문에 많이 나와요. '이웃 나라'는 말투가 더 부드러워요.

phrases.en: It rains a lot in the neighboring area too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바로 옆에 붙은 지역을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an area right next to another.

phrases.en: The fire spread to the adjacent building too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바로 붙어 있는 건물을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a building right next to another.

phrases.en: We are on friendly terms with our neighboring country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인접 국가보다 부드러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer expression than 인접 국가.

explain_en: 인접 is rarely used alone; it attaches to a noun as in '인접 국가', '인접 지역', '인접 건물'. It is stiffer than '옆' or '가까운' and appears in news, maps and official documents; '이웃 나라' (neighbor country) sounds softer.

en: to adjoin; to border on; to be contiguous to

examples.ko: 우리 학교는 큰 공원에 인접해 있어요.
examples.en: Our school is right next to a big park.

examples.ko: 한국은 바다를 사이에 두고 일본과 인접해요.
examples.en: Korea neighbors Japan across the sea.

examples.ko: 인접한 두 방은 벽 하나로 나뉘어 있어요.
examples.en: The two adjoining rooms are divided by a single wall.
Land next to the river is expensive.

examples.ko: 인접하지 않은 지역은 영향을 덜 받았어요.
examples.en: Areas that were not adjacent were less affected.
It borders the road, so it is very noisy.

explain: 'A가 B에 인접하다'처럼 조사 '에'를 써요. 바로 붙어 있거나 아주 가까이 맞닿은 곳에 쓰고, 일상에서는 '옆에 있다', '붙어 있다'가 더 편해요. '인접한 + 명사' 모양으로 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: We trade a lot with neighboring countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인접한' 뒤에 명사를 붙여서 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 인접한 is placed before a noun to describe it.

phrases.en: My house is next to the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual everyday way to say it.

phrases.en: Those two villages are not adjacent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙어 있지 않다는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form: not next to each other.

explain_en: Use the particle '에': 'A가 B에 인접하다'. It is for places that touch or sit very close; in everyday talk '옆에 있다' or '붙어 있다' is easier. The form '인접한 + noun' is very common.

examples.en: My family resides in Seoul.
This area is comfortable for people to live in.

examples.ko: 오래전부터 이 마을에 주거한 사람들을 만났어요.
examples.en: I met people who have lived in this village for a long time.
More people live in high-rise buildings now.
I have no plan to live in the mountains.
He lived abroad and came back last year.

explain: '살다'가 일상 대화의 말이고, 주거하다는 서류·뉴스·부동산 글에서 격식 있게 쓸 때 어울려요. 비슷한 '거주하다'가 더 흔하고, 주거는 '주거 공간', '주거 환경'처럼 명사로 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I reside in Busan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같고 더 흔해서 서류나 뉴스에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning but more common in documents and news.

phrases.en: I moved to a neighborhood with a good living environment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주거'는 명사로 이렇게 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 주거 is more often used as a noun like this.

phrases.en: I decorated my small living space nicely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 사는 집이나 방을 넓게 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broad term for a place where people live.

explain_en: Formal, official: residing in housing, used in documents and notices. '살다' is the everyday word; 주거하다 suits documents, news, and real-estate writing in a formal tone. The similar '거주하다' is more common, and 주거 is used more often as a noun, as in '주거 공간' (living space) and '주거 환경' (living environment).

gh: to live, reside; most common verb

p.n: 산다 is everyday. 주거한다 sounds formal, like a report or document.

examples.en: Our company is in the city center.
The downtown area is too crowded on weekends.
A new department store opened downtown.
It's quiet just a short way out of the city center.

examples.ko: 저는 중심가에 살아서 어디든 가깝지만 시끄러워요.
examples.en: I live downtown so everywhere is close, but it's noisy.

examples.ko: 중심가 식당은 월세가 비싸서 음식값도 비싸요.
examples.en: Restaurants downtown have high rent, so the food is pricey too.

explain: 도시에서 가게와 회사가 가장 많이 모인 번화한 거리를 말해요. '시내'는 도시 안쪽 전체를 가리키는 말이고, '중심가'는 그중 가장 번화한 곳이에요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '시내'를 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I meet my friend downtown on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '중심가'보다 '시내'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk, 시내 is used more often than 중심가.

phrases.en: It's a busy area, so there are many people even at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게와 사람이 많아 복잡하고 활기찬 거리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lively street with many shops and people.

phrases.example: 그 식당은 중심가에 있어서 찾기 쉬워요.
phrases.en: That restaurant is on the main street, so it's easy to find.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 건물의 위치를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to say where a shop or building is.

explain_en: 중심가 is the busiest strip of a city where shops and offices cluster. 시내 refers to the inner city as a whole, and 중심가 is its liveliest part. In everyday talk 시내 is more common.

t90.ax: Our company is in the city center.

examples.en: I'm staying in Seoul for a week.

examples.ko: 외국인이 한국에 오래 체류하려면 비자가 필요해요.
examples.en: Foreigners need a visa to stay in Korea for a long time.
I remember the time I stayed in Busan on a business trip.

examples.ko: 체류 기간이 끝나기 전에 신청해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to apply before your stay period ends.
My friend learned Japanese while staying in Japan.
Next month I'll be staying at a hotel.

explain: 체류하다는 여행보다 공식적인 느낌이 있어서 출입국, 비자, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '지내다', '머무르다'가 더 자연스러워요. 보통 '한국에 체류하다'처럼 장소에 '에'를 붙여요.

phrases.en: I'm staying in Seoul for a week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '체류하다'보다 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than 체류하다 in everyday talk.

phrases.example: 체류 기간이 끝나기 전에 비자를 바꿔야 해요.
phrases.en: I must change my visa before my stay period ends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비자와 출입국 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in talk about visas and immigration.

phrases.en: I'm currently staying in Busan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 어떤 곳에 머물고 있다고 공식적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to say you are staying somewhere now.

explain_en: Formal, staying in a place or country for a period (부산에 체류하다) 체류하다 sounds official and shows up with visas, immigration and the news. In daily talk, people say 지내다 or 머무르다 instead. The place takes 에, as in '한국에 체류하다'.

t90.ax: I'm staying in Seoul for a week.

en: to set sail; to put out to sea; to take wing

examples.ko: 이 항공사는 내년부터 부산에서 도쿄까지 취항해요.
examples.en: This airline will start flying from Busan to Tokyo next year.

examples.ko: 새 여객선이 다음 주에 섬으로 취항할 예정이에요.
examples.en: A new ferry is scheduled to begin service to the island next week.
Airfares got cheaper when a low-cost airline started flying the route.

examples.ko: 첫 취항하는 비행기를 보러 많은 사람이 모였어요.
examples.en: Many people gathered to see the plane making its first flight on the route.
I hope a direct flight starts serving our city.

examples.ko: 오늘 취항한 배를 타고 여행을 다녀왔어요.
examples.en: I went on a trip aboard the ship that began service today.

explain: 주로 항공사나 선박 회사가 새 노선에 처음 다니기 시작할 때 써요. 주어는 보통 '항공사', '비행기', '배'예요. 일상에서는 '새 노선이 생겼어요'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: That airline started flying to Jeju last month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 노선이 시작됐다는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense: the route has already started.

phrases.example: 새 여객선이 다음 달에 섬으로 취항할 예정이에요.
phrases.en: The new ferry is scheduled to start service to the island next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 시작할 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a planned start in the future.

phrases.example: 이 배는 오늘부터 섬까지 운항을 시작해요.
phrases.en: This ship starts operating to the island from today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '취항하다'보다 쉽고 일상적으로 쓰는 같은 뜻의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more everyday way to say the same thing.

explain_en: It is mainly used when an airline or shipping company begins service on a new route. The subject is usually an airline, plane or ship. In daily talk you might also say '새 노선이 생겼어요' (a new route opened).

examples.en: My mother prayed for our family's well-being.
At the end of the letter I wrote, 'I hope you are well.'

examples.ko: 조용한 절에 가니 마음에 평안이 찾아왔어요.
examples.en: Going to the quiet temple brought peace to my mind.
Grandmother sleeps with a peaceful face.
I hope the new year is full of peace for everyone.
He passed away in peace.

explain: 평안은 걱정 없이 마음과 몸이 편안한 상태예요. '편안'은 일상에서 두루 쓰고, '평안'은 인사말, 편지, 종교 글에서 더 자주 보여요. '평안하세요'는 안녕을 비는 정중한 인사로 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I find peace of mind by praying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정 없이 마음이 고요한 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a calm state of mind without worry.

phrases.en: I wished for my family's well-being in the new year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편지나 인사에서 상대의 건강과 안녕을 바랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to wish someone safety and well-being in letters or greetings.

phrases.en: I found peace in the quiet forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 뒤에 마음이 편해지는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the mind becomes calm after a hard time.

explain_en: 평안 is a state of being free from worry, calm in mind and body. 편안 is the everyday word, while 평안 shows up more in greetings, letters and religious writing. 평안하세요 can be used as a polite wish for someone's well-being.

en: to close; to close down; to shut shop

examples.ko: 자주 가던 서점이 다음 달에 폐점해요.
examples.en: The bookstore I often visited is closing down next month.

examples.ko: 손님이 줄어서 결국 가게를 폐점하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Customers dropped off, so we finally decided to close the shop.

examples.ko: 그 체인점은 올해만 열 곳이 폐점했어요.
examples.en: That chain closed ten branches this year alone.
I visited one last time before it closed down.
Regular customers were sad at the news that it was closing.
I will work hard until the day we close.

explain: 가게를 아예 닫고 영업을 끝낸다는 뜻이라서, 하루 일을 마치고 문을 닫는 '문을 닫다'나 '영업을 마치다'와 달라요. 반대말은 '개점하다'이고, 완전히 닫는 경우는 '폐업하다'도 써요. 뉴스와 안내문에 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 이 지점은 이번 달 말에 폐점할 예정이에요.
phrases.en: This branch is going to close at the end of this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 가게를 닫을 계획을 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to announce a planned shop closure.

phrases.example: 문 앞에 폐점 안내가 붙어 있어요.
phrases.en: A notice of closure is posted on the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게 앞이나 홈페이지에 붙는 공지에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen on notices at the shop or on websites.

phrases.en: The restaurant went out of business because sales were poor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 폐점은 가게 하나를 닫는 것이고, 폐업은 사업을 아예 그만두는 것이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 폐점 closes one store, while 폐업 ends the whole business.

explain_en: A shop closes permanently or ends business. It means closing a shop for good and ending business, unlike '문을 닫다' or '영업을 마치다', which can mean just closing for the day. The opposite is '개점하다', and '폐업하다' is also used for a full shutdown. It often appears in news and notices.

t90.ax: I will work hard until the day we close.

examples.en: The ship slowly passes through the narrow strait.
I can see a small island across the strait.

examples.ko: 한국과 일본 사이에는 넓은 해협이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a wide strait between Korea and Japan.
The wind is strong in the strait, so the waves are high.

examples.ko: 다리를 놓아서 해협을 차로 건널 수 있어요.
examples.en: A bridge was built, so you can cross the strait by car.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 해협을 건너는 배가 자주 취소돼요.
examples.en: In winter, ferries crossing the strait are often cancelled.

explain: '대한해협', '도버 해협'처럼 지명 뒤에 붙여 써요. '바다'보다 좁고 양쪽에 땅이 가까운 느낌이에요. 뉴스나 지리 시간에는 자주 나오지만 일상 대화에서는 드물어요.

phrases.en: The Korea Strait is between Korea and Japan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지명 뒤에 '해협'을 붙이는 대표적인 예예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical example of adding 'strait' after a place name.

phrases.en: The ship passed carefully through the narrow strait.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해협의 모양이나 크기를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the shape or size of a strait.

phrases.en: We crossed the strait by boat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해협 건너편으로 간다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for going across to the other side.

explain_en: It attaches after place names, as in '대한해협' and '도버 해협'. It feels narrower than '바다', with land close on both sides. It is common in news and geography class but rare in everyday talk.

en: to be thick and sturdy (of many things)

examples.ko: 이 나무는 가지가 굵직굵직해서 튼튼해 보여요.
examples.en: This tree has thick branches, so it looks sturdy.
Big, major incidents happened one after another this year.
I cut the potatoes into chunky pieces and put them in the stew.

examples.ko: 굵직굵직했던 경기들이 이번 달에 몰려 있어요.
examples.en: The major games are packed into this month.
His finger joints are thick and sturdy.

examples.ko: 굵직굵직하고 단단한 기둥이 지붕을 받치고 있어요.
examples.en: Thick, solid pillars are holding up the roof.

explain: '굵다'와 달리 하나가 아니라 여러 개가 다 굵직할 때 많이 써요. 음식 재료를 큼직하게 썰 때도 쓰고, '굵직굵직한 사건', '굵직굵직한 작품'처럼 중요하고 큰 일이 여러 개일 때도 써요.

phrases.en: Please cut the potatoes into thick chunks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리에서 재료를 큼직하게 썰 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in cooking for cutting ingredients thick and large.

phrases.example: 이 감독은 굵직굵직한 작품을 많이 만들었어요.
phrases.en: This director made many major works.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크고 중요한 작품이 여러 개일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when there are many large, important works.

phrases.en: These branches are all thick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 개가 모두 굵을 때 해요체로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite form for when many things are all thick.

explain_en: Unlike plain '굵다', it is often used when several things are all thick. It is used for chunky-cut ingredients, and also for several big, important things, as in '굵직굵직한 사건' (major incidents) or '굵직굵직한 작품' (major works).

t90.ax: His finger joints are thick and sturdy.

examples.en: This problem needs a multifaceted approach.
The teacher evaluates students from multiple perspectives.

examples.ko: 다면적 분석을 해야 정확한 결과가 나와요.
examples.en: You need a multifaceted analysis to get accurate results.

examples.ko: 그는 다면적 성격을 가진 사람이라 알기 어려워요.
examples.en: He has a many-sided personality, so he's hard to figure out.

examples.ko: 회사는 직원을 다면적 평가 방식으로 심사해요.
examples.en: The company reviews employees through a multi-angle evaluation method.

examples.ko: 그 사건에는 다면적 원인이 얽혀 있어요.
examples.en: Many different causes are tangled up in that incident.

explain: '다면적 평가', '다면적 접근', '다면적 분석'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여 써요. 서술어로 말할 때는 '다면적이다'나 '다면적인'으로도 쓸 수 있어요. 비슷한 '다각적'은 여러 방향에서 본다는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: The school introduced a multifaceted evaluation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지가 아니라 여러 면을 보고 판단할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when judging by several aspects rather than just one.

phrases.en: We need to look at the problem from many sides.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사처럼 '다면적으로'를 써서 동사를 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: '다면적으로' works like an adverb to modify a verb.

phrases.en: This is a topic that needs multifaceted analysis.
phrases.nuance_ko: '다면적이다'의 꾸밈형이라, 명사 앞에서 '다면적'과 같은 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifying form of '다면적이다', meaning the same as '다면적' before a noun.

explain_en: It is placed before a noun, as in '다면적 평가', '다면적 접근' and '다면적 분석'. As a predicate you can also say '다면적이다' or '다면적인'. The similar '다각적' has a stronger feeling of looking from several directions.

t90.ax: This problem needs a multifaceted approach.

examples.ko: 정수리 쪽 머리카락이 듬성듬성 나 있어요.
examples.en: The hair on the crown of my head is growing thinly.
I scattered lettuce seeds sparsely in the garden plot.
The students are sitting spread out in the classroom.
His beard is patchy, so he looks untidy.
I walked along a road with patches of snow here and there.

examples.ko: 옷에 흰 털이 듬성듬성 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: There are white hairs stuck here and there on your clothes.

explain: 사이가 성기게 드문드문 있는 모양을 말해요. 반대는 '빽빽이', '촘촘히'예요. '띄엄띄엄'은 시간 간격에도 쓰지만 '듬성듬성'은 머리카락·씨앗·사람처럼 공간에서 드물게 있을 때 써요.

phrases.example: 며칠 못 깎았더니 수염이 듬성듬성 났어요.
phrases.en: I haven't shaved for a few days, so my beard has come in sparsely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리카락·수염·풀처럼 무언가가 드물게 자라는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when hair, beard, or grass grows in thinly with gaps.

phrases.example: 모종을 듬성듬성 심어서 밭이 휑해 보여요.
phrases.en: The seedlings were planted far apart, so the field looks bare.
phrases.nuance_ko: 씨앗이나 모종을 간격을 넓게 둘 때 써요. 반대로 간격이 좁으면 '촘촘히 심다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when seeds or seedlings are planted with wide gaps; the opposite is '촘촘히 심다'.

phrases.example: 비 오는 날이라 극장에 사람들이 듬성듬성 앉아 있어요.
phrases.en: It's a rainy day, so people are sitting scattered around the theater.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 드문드문 떨어져 앉은 모습을 말해요. 자리가 많이 비어 있다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes people sitting spread out with many empty seats between them.

explain_en: Things placed far apart in space, like seeds, hair, or stitches. It describes things placed or growing far apart with gaps between them. Its opposites are '빽빽이' and '촘촘히' (densely). '띄엄띄엄' can also describe time intervals, but '듬성듬성' is for things sparse in space, like hair, seeds or people.

t90.ax: His beard is patchy, so he looks untidy.

examples.en: A can is shaped like a cylinder.
I solved a problem about finding the volume of a cylinder.
A cylinder has round top and bottom faces.
This container looks like a cylinder.
If you lay a cylinder on its side, it rolls easily.
In math class, we made a cylinder out of paper.

explain: 수학 시간에 주로 쓰는 말이고, 일상에서는 '통 모양'이라고 말하기도 해요. 같이 배우는 도형으로 '원뿔', '각기둥'이 있어요.

phrases.en: This container is cylinder-shaped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건의 모양을 설명할 때 '모양'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 모양 describes the shape of an object.

phrases.en: Try drawing a cylinder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수학이나 미술 시간에 도형을 그리라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in math or art class when asked to draw a shape.

phrases.en: A toilet paper roll is tube-shaped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '원기둥'을 쉽게 바꿔 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday, easier way to say cylinder.

explain_en: It is mostly a math-class word; in daily life people may say '통 모양' (tube shape). Shapes studied alongside it include '원뿔' (cone) and '각기둥' (prism).

examples.ko: 졸업식 날 학생들은 모두 검은 옷 일색이었어요.
examples.en: On graduation day the students were all in black.

examples.ko: 이 동네 가게는 치킨집 일색이라 다른 음식이 그리워요.
examples.en: The shops in this neighborhood are all chicken places, so I miss other food.
The meeting room was all men, so it felt a little awkward.

examples.ko: 응원 온 사람들이 붉은색 일색으로 입고 왔어요.
examples.en: The people who came to cheer all wore red.

examples.ko: 비슷한 건물 일색인 거리를 걷다 보니 지루해졌어요.
examples.en: Walking along the street of nothing but similar buildings got boring.
These days TV is all about food.

explain: '흰색 일색', '남자 일색'처럼 앞에 색이나 사람, 사물을 붙여서 한 가지로만 채워진 모습을 말해요. '일색이다'처럼 서술어로도 쓰고, 다양하지 않다는 느낌이 들 때가 많아요.

phrases.example: 눈이 와서 온 세상이 흰색 일색이에요.
phrases.en: It snowed, so the whole world is nothing but white.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지 색으로만 가득할 때 색 이름 뒤에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached after a color name when everything is filled with just that one color.

phrases.en: The meeting room was all men, so it felt a little awkward.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 앞에 붙이면 한 종류의 사람만 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: After a word for people, it means only one kind of person is present.

phrases.en: The shops in this neighborhood are all cafes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서술어로 써서 한 가지뿐이라 다양하지 않다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a predicate, it suggests there is only one kind and little variety.

explain_en: You attach a color, a type of person or a thing before it, as in '흰색 일색' or '남자 일색', to say something is filled with just one kind. It can also be used as a predicate, '일색이다', and it often suggests a lack of variety.

en: to be tiny; to be trivial

examples.en: The writing is so tiny that it is hard to read.
There were lots of little tasks, so I was busy again today.
I picked up tiny shells at the beach.
Please chop the onion finely and add it.
The small worries I had are nothing now.
Even if the expenses are small, they add up to a lot.

explain: '작다'와 달리 작은 것들이 여럿 모여 있을 때 어울려요. '자잘한 글씨, 자잘한 일'처럼 쓰고, 일에 쓰면 '사소한'에 가까워요. 비슷한 말로 '자질구레하다'도 있어요.

phrases.en: Tiny flowers bloomed all over the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 꽃이 여러 송이 모여 있는 모습에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits many small flowers growing together.

phrases.en: There were many small mistakes, so I checked again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크지 않지만 여러 번 생기는 사소한 잘못에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for minor mistakes that are not big but happen many times.

phrases.en: After moving, there are lots of little chores.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이지만 쓸모없고 하찮은 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word, but with a stronger sense of petty or trivial.

explain_en: Many small, fine pieces; also trivial things (자잘한 알갱이) Unlike '작다', it fits when many small things are gathered together, as in '자잘한 글씨' or '자잘한 일'. Used for tasks it means 'trivial'. A similar word is '자질구레하다'.

t90.ax: I picked up tiny shells at the beach.
